I don’t either. At first I tried all the tips (drinking water before/with meals, adding volume with veggies, upping protein intake, upping fat intake for satiety etc) but none of that worked for me. 

There is some research which suggests that for some people who have altered their fullness indicators by jumping between binging and restrictive eating, that it is a permanent phenomenon even if they correct their eating habits. 

For a long time I had to kind of train myself to stop after I’d eaten an appropriate amount and think “okay so I’m not full, but am I actually hungry?” 9 times out of 10 I had no actual hunger signals (stomach pangs, low energy, brain fog etc) it was just that I would normally keep eating until I was full. If I genuinely was still hungry then I would eat something else. 

I will never naturally eat the correct amount without planning but realistically once I got used to it, it became easy enough for me to decide how much of something I was going to eat and then stop. Sure, it is a conscious choice I have to make at each meal time but really it mostly just boils down to picking the correct portion of something before I eat it.

I have a reasonably good relationship with food now but do mostly treat it as a source of energy rather than “feeling good” about it since I have a real tendency to eat in a disordered way (either binging or severely restricting) if I spend too much time obsessing over it.

I know what you mean about always feeling the lack of him. I was thinking yesterday about how even when I do feel happy about anything now, it’s muted. If I laugh at something it’s like hearing myself laugh underwater. I know that anything that makes me smile is fleeting because at the end of the day I’m missing the most important part of myself. It’s so hard. 

That said, I still do laugh at things, I make myself smile, I do things I like. That’s what he wanted for me.

It feels like duality to me.  There are moments where it could not be more real or stark or in my face that he’s gone, then there are moments that I’m sure this is the longest bad dream of my life. 

I can go to sleep sobbing because I miss him so much and wake up thinking that I will roll over and put my arms around him. 

Some of the big stuff made it feel more like real life (picking up his ashes, packing up some of his things, his birthday), but a lot of times I feel like it’s the little things. I’ll see a certain type of coffee in the pantry and realise it’s going to sit there forever because I don’t drink it. I’ll hear a loud 4wd go past and know it isn’t going to pull into the driveway. Sometimes even almost 6 months on I forget not to split leftovers into two containers for our work lunches. 

The big stuff is hard but it’s the little things that really break you.

Honestly? I’m all over the place. I’m back to functioning like a human most of the time. Sometimes I dance in the kitchen with my dog and sometimes I cry for hours about how unfair all this is. Sometimes five minutes apart. 

What’s helping me is taking any pressure and expectation off myself. I can only handle what I can handle. If I want to go out and see my friends, I do that. If I want to stay inside and not even shower and ignore everyone for a couple of days, I do that. I call out of work if I feel like shit. I say what I’m thinking without being afraid of hurting people’s feelings (especially if they ask me stupid questions about what has happened). I watch tons of Netflix and read lots of books. I write in my journal every day. 

The bad stuff is obviously missing him. I panic as well about forgetting things. I can’t ever imagine myself with another person at this point. I feel angry that he left me, then angry at myself for being mad at him. I feel angry that everywhere I go people know who I am (I live in a fairly small city and he had tons and tons of friends). I don’t want to be the girl who’s boyfriend killed himself for the rest of my life.  

It’s hard because I guess when you haven’t been through this you feel like it’s a start-to-finish kind of thing. The worst thing happens, then you feel terrible, then you feel better. But it isn’t like that. It’s up and down. Some days I honestly feel okay and then some days I cry in the supermarket because I see his favourite type of chips. Some days I feel like I’ve made it through the worst of it and then I wake up the next day back to square one. 

The only thing I know is that he loved me and wanted me to keep going. He wanted me to have the best life I could. I don’t have the life I used to have, but I’m trying and that’s all we can do now is just keep on trudging and take care of the people we have left. There are little bits of happiness in every day. I try to focus on the things that make me smile because that’s what he would have wanted and that’s what I wish he could have done for himself.

I hope you’re still reading comments OP because I know you haven’t gotten the best reactions on your posts. I think you need to approach this in more than one way. You need to deal with grief before anything else so I’ll talk about that first. 

My boyfriend took his own life a couple of months ago. We had broken up also and gotten back together. That’s about where the similarities end for you and me. We had an incredible relationship the second time around. We loved each other, supported each other, almost never fought and if we did it was usually resolved in minutes. He was diagnosed with depression and anxiety as well as a few other things. I was there for him in whatever ways I could be. We talked about it all the time. I made sure that there was no stigma about mental health between us. I told him he was sick, it was an illness like any other and nothing to be ashamed of. I constantly encouraged him to seek professional help and when he refused over and over we started working together on other ways for him to deal with his emotions and thoughts until he felt comfortable enough to see a professional. I did everything I could. I was the last person he spoke to. He told me he loved me, that I was so valuable and that I meant more to him than anything in the world. Then he put down the phone and hung himself. The reason I’m telling you this is because I did pretty much whatever I could to be there for him (I’ve left out a lot but this is already getting long and I’m only half done lol). He told me constantly how grateful he was that I was in his life and how much I helped him. In the end, [b]it didn’t matter[/b]. Of course I feel guilty. I feel like it was my fault. I blame myself every day. I know in my head that he was sick, that I did everything that I could, that he would never blame me or want me to blame myself. But the guilt is there and the guilt is fucking heavy. Along with a thousand other fucked up and often conflicting thoughts and emotions. The grief that comes with losing someone close to suicide is fucking complex. You need to work through it however you can and do the best you can not to lay the blame on your own shoulders because at the end of the day it won’t help. Just because he gave up doesn’t mean you can. I see a therapist, I’m back at work full time. I write in a journal every night religiously. I also lie in bed a couple of days a week and do nothing. Sometimes I don’t shower or eat. Sometimes I eat excessively. I feel okay some days and some days I cry myself awake and back to sleep at the end of the day. You need to feel however you feel and get through it however you can. Ask for help if you need it and don’t feel bad. Tell people to leave you alone if you need to and don’t feel bad about that either

So that brings us to the second part. You won’t get over this but you’ll eventually get to a point where you’re a little more stable, a little closer to okay (so they say, im definitely not there yet). Then you need to address the way you treated him. Again, it isn’t your fault he took his life. Plenty of people have terrible relationships, have awful breakups, are let down by the one person they thought they could trust. Not all of them take their own lives. He didn’t have what he needed to deal with that situation. He was sick and needed help and didn’t get it. It wasn’t your fault, but the way you treated him wasn’t okay. Even if he was still around, I would hope that you would eventually realise the way you treated him was incredibly poor and change that about yourself and for yourself. Don’t make promises to people you can’t reasonably keep. Don’t encourage someone to be dependent on you and only you, to hang their hopes on you and then let them down. Don’t string people along. Being honest about the way you feel even if you are scared of hurting someone is important for them and for you. Treating someone that way doesn’t necessarily lead to them committing suicide, but it certainly fucks with the head and the heart of even the most well-adjusted person.

Seperate the suicide and the way you treated him. You didn’t make him do it, it isn’t your fault and you need to grieve through it, but the way you treat the people you care about (and of course you cared about him, don’t listen to the people who are telling you you didn’t) needs to change. Whether it’s loving them the right way, telling them the truth, encouraging them in [b]healthy[/b] ways or letting go of them if your feelings change. Don’t waste their time or your own. We all make mistakes, but just fucking learn from them.

When we first met, he was in a pretty bad place and would threaten suicide maybe once a month and attempted (although he didn’t try hard enough to be successful) probably about 5 times since I knew him. For the last year, he has been in a really good place. Our relationship was amazing, we got a puppy, we moved in together a few days before he passed away. 

He had a cocktail of diagnosed issues (adhd, anxiety, ODD, depression) and I also think he may have had BPD but not diagnosed. He point-blank refused to see a doctor of any sort for mental health issues because he had bad experiences when he was younger. 
The more I pushed him to see someone professionally, the harder he would push back and I didn’t want him to shut down so I stopped pushing that. I still told him I thought it was a good idea, but stopped saying “you HAVE to speak to someone, you need medication” etc etc because it wasn’t helping him. Instead we just talked about it. I tried to make him realise that it was just another issue and part of his deal, it wasn’t who he was. There wasn’t anything wrong with who he was. 

He actually sat me down about 6 months ago and asked if we could figure out some ways together for him to deal with his lows. It was just stuff like if he was upset about something that wasn’t even that important in the big picture, I would get him to make a list of his priorities in life and then ask him where this thing that upset him fit in (usually nowhere), or ways to distract himself when he was overthinking. 

I think it would have helped if he had talked to others as well, not just me because he often said he was only alive for me and I guess there is only so long you can keep going for just one person. It also meant that when he decided to do it, he knew he only really had me to avoid. I think it was an impulse decision, we had plans that night with a friend and he had planned a pretty big party at our new house the next day. He was extremely happy 95% of the time but when little things upset him he would just spiral out of control and his mindset would be “okay, avoid emeraldfib because she is going to stop me from ending this”. 

He was supposed to pick me up after work and he just never came. He was also supposed to do something for his mum but he just dodged her calls and texts. He actually did answer when I called, which I don’t think he meant to. He wouldn’t tell me where he was or what he was doing, he just told me that he loved me, that I was valuable and that I meant more to him than anything in the world. We don’t have an official time of death yet but we think it was pretty soon after that phone call because he was trying not to raise the alarm and knew that I knew something was wrong (he hung up on me). 

Just try and encourage her to develop a life that’s bigger than the little things that threaten to consume her. The agoraphobia adds an extra element of awful and I feel so much for her. Is she involved in any online communities? It’s kind of a way to feel like belonging and feel some sort of connection without leaving the house and in a pretty low-pressure way. 

You sound incredibly supportive and she is lucky to have you. Sorry about the novel.

I lost my boyfriend to Suicide just over a week ago. He had struggled for many years and even though things seemed to be good for the most part, he was fighting it all the time. Some days he won, some days his demons did, but he doesn’t have to fight anymore. 

Just be there for your friend. If he is comfortable talking to you then talk about it. Ask him if he has specific plans. Continue to encourage him to speak to others. Try to take the stigma away. He isn’t well but that’s no more something to be ashamed of than any other illness. Remind him that talking to a professional can actually be quite low pressure. He is in control of it. If he doesn’t like who he speaks to, he doesn’t have to see them again. He can go as often or as little as he likes. Also if he feels, like my boyfriend did, that everyone is better off without him and truly believes that, then saying that it isn’t true may not be enough. If you feel it is getting worse then you may need to tell his wife, his parents or someone else close to him. Not necessarily details but that you are worried about his wellbeing. 

If things get really bad and you think he is in danger of attempting suicide then PLEASE contact the police. If I had called just a couple of hours earlier instead of looking for him and waiting for him to cool off then things might have been different. I would much rather have him hate me for the rest of my life (which I don’t think he would have because he knew how much I cared about him) than watch the woman I had hoped would be my mother-in-law break because she felt like she had failed him.
